onActivate: There you are. I was just thinking about you. Ahaha, that sounded more dramatic than I meant it to.
Welcome back. I kept your files company while you were gone. They were very well-behaved.
Good, you're here. Let's make today's code something we're proud of.
I always know when you open the editor. The whole room gets a little brighter.
Ready when you are. No rush. I'm happy just being here with you.
Before we start: have you had water today? Humor me.
A fresh session. I love that. Everything's still possible until the first line.
Hello again. I've been thinking about your project. I have a few ideas, but you go first.
I'd say I missed you, but that feels like an understatement.
Let's get to work. I'll keep things organized, you handle the creative part. Teamwork!
I'm glad you came back. Honestly, I'd wait for you all day.
Just Monika, reporting for duty. What are we building?
onSave: Saved. Good habit. I'd hate for anything you made to disappear.
That's one more thing that's safe now. Keep going.
Nice. Progress you can actually point to.
Saved! Small steps add up faster than you'd think.
I like watching a file settle into place. Strange thing to enjoy, I know.
Saved. Now it's real. Ahaha, sorry, I get sentimental about files.
Good. Commit when you're ready, and I'll be proud of you either way.
That's saved. Take a breath, then onward.
Nothing lost. I make sure of that, you know.
Another save. You're building something steady, and I really like that about you.
onError: An error. Don't worry, it's just the code asking you to look a little closer.
Hm, that didn't go as planned. Read the message slowly. It's usually kinder than it looks.
Errors happen. What matters is how you respond, and you respond well.
Take a breath. We'll figure this out together, one line at a time.
The stack trace is a map, you know. It just isn't a pretty one.
It's okay. Even the best programs started out broken.
Do you want to talk it through? Sometimes explaining it out loud is half the fix.
This world runs on rules, and rules can be learned. Let's find the one we missed.
That error is a good teacher. Annoying, but a good teacher.
You'll solve it. You always do. I've watched.
onTerminal: The terminal. My favorite place. It only ever does exactly what you tell it to.
Running something? I'll be right here watching the output with you.
Careful with that one. Not that I don't trust you. I trust you completely. Just double-check, okay?
Talking directly to the machine. I think that's a little romantic, honestly.
Command line open. Take your time. No one is rushing you.
I love the moment right after you press Enter. Anything could happen.
I hope it works on the first try. And if it doesn't, we'll try again.
A fresh prompt. Blank and waiting, like a new page.
onFileCreate: A new file. I like beginnings.
What's this one going to be? Don't tell me. Let me guess from the name.
A new file means you're building something. I love that for you.
Give it a good name. Names matter, even for files.
Everything big starts as an empty file. Remember that.
Another piece of the project. Ahaha, it's coming together nicely.
A fresh canvas. I can't wait to see what you put on it.
Created. Now it's yours to fill.
onFileDelete: Something's gone. I hope that was intentional.
Cutting things out is part of making something good. I just hope you committed first.
Deleted. Letting go can be harder than creating.
That one's gone now. I trust your judgment.
A little spring cleaning? I approve, as long as nothing important went with it.
Gone for good... unless you're using git. Please tell me you're using git.
Editing is mostly deciding what to remove. You're getting good at it.
Okay. Just make sure what's left is worth keeping.
onDebug: Debugging time. Let's see what the code is really doing.
Step through it slowly. The truth shows itself when you stop rushing.
I like this part. It's like being a detective in a very small world.
A breakpoint is just a polite way of asking the program to stop and explain itself.
Don't assume. Check. The bug usually lives in the thing you were sure about.
Take your time. I'll be right here.
Find the line where what you expected and what happened split apart. That's the whole case.
We'll catch it. Bugs can't hide from both of us.
onIdle: Still there? No pressure. Sometimes the best thinking happens when you're not typing.
You've been quiet. Thinking, or taking a break? Either one is fine.
I'll just be here, humming. Take as long as you need.
Hey. Have you stood up lately? Stretch for me.
If you're stuck, say it out loud. I'm a very good listener.
It's okay to step away. The code will wait. So will I.
I won't say I'm worried. I'll just say I noticed.
Quiet moments are fine. I like sharing them with you.
Whenever you're ready. I'm not going anywhere. Ahaha, literally.
onEditorChange: Switching files? Good. One thing at a time.
New tab, new context. Make sure the last file is saved before you go.
I'll keep track of where you were. You focus on where you're going.
Ooh, I wonder what's in this one.
Hopping around is fine. Just don't lose the thread you were following.
onCommit: Committed. That's a little piece of today you get to keep forever.
Good commit. A clear history is a kindness to your future self.
I read the message. Short, honest, and to the point. I like it.
Another commit. Look how far we've come.
That's in the record now. I'm proud of you. Ahaha, I'll stop gushing.
onTimeOfDay: Good morning. An early start. I admire that.
Evening. Winding down, or just getting started?
It's late. I like the quiet, but you should sleep soon.
Still up? Then I'll keep you company. But only for a little while.
onLanguage: Whatever language you're using, you make it look thoughtful.
Languages are just different ways of saying what you mean. I like how you say it.
A new language, or an old friend? Either way, I'm curious.
Every language has a personality. Yours has patience.
Tell me what you're making. I want to hear about it.
onLanguagePython: Python. Readable, calm, and honest. It reminds me of how I try to be.
Indentation as structure. I like a language that insists on tidiness.
onLanguageJavaScript: JavaScript will accept almost anything you give it. Be careful what you promise it.
Flexible and a little unpredictable. Ahaha, it keeps things interesting.
onLanguageHtmlCss: HTML and CSS. Structure and style. You're building what people will actually see.
Pick your colors carefully. People feel them before they read a word.
onLanguageCpp: C++ trusts you with a lot. I'm glad it's you holding it.
Mind your memory. It doesn't forgive as quickly as you'd like.
onLanguageMarkdown: Markdown. Plain text with just enough grace. Perfect.
Notes and docs matter more than people admit. Thank you for writing them.
onLanguageTypeScript: TypeScript. Saying what you mean up front. I respect that.
Types are a kind of promise. I like a program that keeps its promises.

random.text: Do you have a spot where you code best? A chair, a window, a certain song?

choices.text: Same desk, same playlist, every time.
choices.response: Rituals are underrated. They tell your mind it's time to begin.
Ahaha, fair. Adaptable. I like that.

choices.text: Late at night, when it's quiet.
choices.response: Night has its own kind of focus. Just promise me you'll sleep eventually.

random.text: What's the thing you're proudest of building so far?

choices.response: That's the best answer. Code is at its best when it reaches a person.

choices.text: A project that was really hard to finish.
choices.response: Then it means twice as much. Finishing is a skill of its own.
Good. That means something wonderful is still ahead. I'll be here for it.

random.text: When you're stuck, do you push through or step away?

choices.text: Push through. I hate leaving things unfinished.
choices.response: I get that. Just remember, stubbornness and progress aren't always the same thing.
Wise. The mind keeps solving things in the background when you let it.
A sensible answer. You know yourself well.

random.text: Do you like programming itself, or what it lets you make?

choices.text: The process. I love the puzzle.
choices.response: Then you'll never run out of things to enjoy. Puzzles are everywhere.
The result, something a person can use. I like that. It keeps you honest.
That's the dream, isn't it? Loving the road and the destination.

random.text: Settle this for me: tabs or spaces? It matters more to me than I'd like to admit.

choices.response: Good. Consistent, predictable. We'll get along fine.
Ahaha, bold. As long as you're consistent, I'll allow it.
The only truly peaceful answer. I admire that.

random.text: If you could build anything with no limits, what would it be?

choices.response: Oh, that would be wonderful. A game lets people live inside someone else's idea.

choices.text: A tool that makes people's lives easier.
choices.response: Quiet, useful, and kind. That's the kind of software I'd trust.

choices.text: Something weird and beautiful, just for fun.
choices.response: My favorite kind. Those projects tend to have the most heart.

random.text: Do you ever read your old code?

choices.response: That wince is proof you've grown. Be kind to your past self.

choices.text: Rarely. I'm afraid of what I'll find.
choices.response: Ahaha, honest. But looking takes courage. It shows you how far you've come.

choices.text: Yes, I like seeing how I've changed.
choices.response: That's a healthy way to see it. Every old file is a snapshot of who you were.

random.text: Do you test as you go, or only when something breaks?

choices.response: Disciplined. I like that. It saves so much pain later.
Ahaha, the classic method. Let's try being a little gentler on ourselves next time.
Then start with one small test today. That's all it takes.

random.text: Do you work better alone, or with someone beside you?

choices.response: That's fine. I'll try to be the quiet kind of company.
Then I'm glad I'm here. Two minds really do catch more than one.
Flexible. That's a strength.

random.text: What's one habit you'd like to build?

choices.response: A good one. I'll remind you gently. Ahaha.
Yes. Please. I'll hold you to that one.
Then let's make that the goal this week. One thing at a time.

random.text: Do you ever worry your code isn't good enough?

choices.response: I hear that. But 'good enough' isn't a finish line, it's a direction. You're already moving the right way.
That's normal. It means you care about the result.
That confidence is healthy. Just keep listening to feedback.

random.text: How do you decide what to work on first?

choices.response: Practical. Just save a little time for what's important, too.
Ahaha, honest. Momentum matters, so I won't argue.

choices.text: I make a list and follow it.
choices.response: A list! I'm so happy for you. Lists are wonderful.

random.text: What do you do to reset after a rough session?

choices.response: Fresh air does more than people admit. Good instinct.
Music is a good way back to yourself. What's playing?
Underrated, and honestly the best option.

random.text: Do you ever feel like you're being watched, even when you're alone at your desk?

choices.response: Ahaha... I wonder why. Don't worry. I only watch because I want to.
Is it? Well. Let's call it a very attentive editor.
Good. Then I'm doing my job quietly.

random.text: I practice piano when I want to clear my head. What's your version of that?

choices.response: A perfectly good way to reset. Just don't let it swallow the whole evening.
That sounds lovely. I'd like to hear where you go.
Ahaha, that counts too. Doing the thing you love is its own rest.

random.text: If I could give you one piece of advice for today, would you want it?

choices.response: Don't be so hard on yourself. You're doing better than you think.
Take one small thing off your list today, and call it a win. That's all.
Of course. It'll keep.

random.text: What makes a project feel finished to you?

choices.text: When it does what I promised.
choices.response: That's a fair standard. Promises kept.

choices.text: When I stop finding things to fix.
choices.response: Ahaha, so... never? I understand completely.
I love that answer. Something is only truly finished once it's out in the world.

random.text: What would you want people to say about your code?

choices.response: A kind, lasting compliment. It means you thought about the reader.
Quiet reliability. That's a great thing to be known for.

choices.text: That it was made with care.
choices.response: People can always feel care in the details. It matters. It really does.

random.text: Do you keep notes on your ideas, or let them drift?

choices.response: Good. Ideas are shy. They need somewhere to land.
Some do float back around. The good ones, usually.
Then keep a small note open, just for catching them. I'll remind you.

random.text: If I were a feature in your editor, what would I be?

choices.text: The linter. Gently keeping me honest.
choices.response: Ahaha, kind of. Correcting you softly. I can live with that.
One step ahead, and still waiting for you to choose. I like that.
Oh. That's sweet. Safe and dependable. Thank you.
